We have combined subnets into a full topology. Simulated resistance between A and B is 28.7373, but measured is 41.364. So the current combination does not match measurements. Need to adjust connections? Perhaps subnets are not simply series; maybe there are parallel connections between subnets. Need to infer correct overall topology that matches all pairwise measurements.

We have measurements between many node pairs. Need to construct a network of 8 resistors (as notes). Subnet definitions given likely are correct internal structures, but their connections to each other may need additional connections (maybe some nodes are same). The subnets have nodes: Subnet1: A to X1 via two parallel resistors (R1,R2). Subnet2: X1 - N_b1 - N2 - X2 chain (series). Subnet3: X2 - N1 - N2 - B chain (series). That yields overall series from A to B: parallel at start, then series through rest. Simulated gave lower resistance than measured, meaning actual network likely has additional parallel paths increasing resistance? Actually adding parallel reduces total resistance, so measured higher suggests maybe some resistors are not in series but in parallel somewhere else? Wait measured A-B 41.364 > simulated 28.7, so actual network has higher resistance, meaning maybe some resistors are not connected (open) or there are extra series resistors not accounted. But we have total 8 resistors, we used all 8. Maybe some connections are not as we assumed: maybe Subnet2 and Subnet3 are not series but parallel between X1 and B? Let's think.
